course: While the course itself is great and has allowed me many opportunities to grow and develop my writing, I do wish we could read more, too. We read six stories and held discussions on them, five of which were student-led, then the rest of the weeks were reading and commentating on peer writing, which is not a bad activity at all, and peer advice can really help when it comes to viewing your work from different perspectives and getting feedback and advice, I feel like, at least for those who wanted it, continuing to read more stories from outside the classroom and having discussions on them (written would have been great too, like on Moodle, considering there likely is not enough class time if a great reduction in student count per section). I also don't think this course should have been mandatory. It causes a lot of people to take it who clearly do not want to be there, while a certain section of the class have great interest in the subject and pretty much "carry" it for everyone else. But that also means there's a lot of precious time wasted reading their stories when they really don't want to be doing any of it anyway. If it became an elective, so only those who really were passionate could take the course, they could read stories and hold discussions, and provide peer feedback in a matter where everyone could engage and the class hours would be as efficient as they could ever be. I also didn't really get, for a course titled creative *writing*, why there was so much public speaking. It was difficult to be discussion leaders. In general, though, for people with interest in creative writing (and discussing creative works), it's quite pleasant and fun to take, and I would absolutely take it again. Especially for those with little experience sharing their writing beforehand, like myself, it can help gain that confidence and learn a lot about how people may interpret their work. I genuinely believe what I learned here will continue to benefit me in my writing journey.
